title: 2023 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: When the roots of the polynomial \[P(x) = (x-1)^1(x-2)^2(x-3)^3 \cdots (x-10)^{10}\] are removed from the real number line, what remains is the union of \(11\) disjoint open intervals. On how many of those intervals is \(P(x)\) positive?

solutions.text: For \(x \gt 10,\) every factor \((x - i)^i\) is positive, so \(P(x) \gt 0.\) Now move left. Crossing \(x = i\) flips the sign only when \(i\) is odd, that is at \(i = 9, 7, 5, 3, 1.\) So the eleven intervals, right to left, carry signs \(+, +, -, -, +, +, -, -, +, +, -.\) Six are positive. Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: For \(x \gt 10\) every factor is positive; the sign of \(P\) can only change at a root
Crossing the root \(x = i\) flips the sign exactly when the exponent \(i\) is odd
